title: Indian-Origin Teenagers Shreyas Royal and Bodhana Sivanandan Win 2026 British Chess Championships
excerpt: Shreyas Royal, 17, becomes the youngest British Chess Champion in history while 11-year-old Bodhana Sivanandan claims the Women's title at the record-breaking Coventry event.
body:
• Shreyas Royal, 17, won the 2026 British Chess Championship at Coventry, becoming the youngest champion in the tournament's 122-year history, surpassing Michael Adams's 1989 record.
  • Bodhana Sivanandan, 11, won the Women's British Chess Championship after a rapid playoff, becoming the youngest women's champion ever.
  • Both players have Indian-origin families — Royal's parents are from India and nearly had to leave the UK over a visa dispute in 2018, while Sivanandan's parents moved from Tiruchirappalli, Tamil Nadu, to London in 2007.
  • The 112th British Chess Championships drew more than 1,700 entries, a record for the event, held at the University of Warwick from August 1 to 9.

Royal Becomes Youngest British Champion

Shreyas Royal claimed the 2026 British Chess Championship title at the University of Warwick in Coventry, completing a nine-round tournament that ran from August 1 to 9. At 17 years and 7 months old, he broke a record that had stood for 37 years — Michael Adams won the title in 1989 at 17 years, 8 months, and 25 days.

https://x.com/toisports/status/2086771606165356704

Royal, who plays for England and holds the grandmaster title, entered the 106-player championship as the second seed behind Luke McShane. The Indian-origin teenager from London has been on a rapid ascent since becoming England's youngest International Master in 2021 and the youngest British grandmaster in history in August 2024.

His path to the championship was years in the making but nearly didn't happen. In 2018, Royal's family faced deportation when his father's work visa was set to expire. An online petition gathered thousands of signatures, and the Home Office granted a new visa just weeks before the deadline, according to reports at the time. Royal had moved to England from India as a young child.

Sivanandan Wins Women's Title at 11

Bodhana Sivanandan won the Women's British Chess Championship after finishing the main event tied on 5½ out of 9 points with Trisha Kanyamarala, then winning the rapid playoff 1½–½ to take the title outright. At 11 years old, she became the youngest women's champion in the history of the event, according to FIDE.

"It is an extraordinary rise for a Harrow schoolgirl who took up the game during lockdown after finding a chessboard and set in a bag her father wanted to throw out."

— English Chess Federation

Sivanandan's parents moved from Tiruchirappalli in Tamil Nadu to England in 2007. She was born in London in 2015 and started playing chess during the COVID-19 lockdown in 2020, after discovering a chess set her father had been about to discard. Within six years, she went from complete beginner to Britain's top-rated female player.

Her 2026 record has been staggering. In April, she became England's number one ranked female player with a FIDE rating of 2366, overtaking four-time champion Lan Yao. In July, she became the youngest girl ever to defeat a grandmaster rated above 2600, beating Marc'Andria Maurizzi. That same month, she broke Judit Polgár's 38-year-old record by becoming the youngest girl to achieve an International Master norm, at 11 years and 4 months — Polgár had done it at 11 years and 9 months in 1988.

A Record-Breaking Championship

The 112th British Chess Championships attracted more than 1,700 entries across all sections — the largest in the event's 122-year history, which dates to 1904. A record £34,000 prize fund was on offer in the main championship, and the women's prize fund more than doubled from previous years.

Top seed Luke McShane and nine-time champion Michael Adams were among the field, with Adams seeking to equal Jonathan Penrose's record of 10 titles. The tournament featured age-group events from under-8 to seniors alongside the main championship.

The English Chess Federation expanded the festival's programming, adding training sessions for junior players and a broader range of social events. Commentary was streamed live on YouTube with analysis from Grandmasters Daniel Gormally and Nick Pert.

Diaspora Prodigies on a Global Stage

The dual Indian-origin victory at Britain's most prestigious chess event reflects a broader trend of diaspora children excelling in competitive chess worldwide. Royal's journey from a family facing visa uncertainty to becoming British champion is a particularly striking arc.

Sivanandan, meanwhile, has drawn comparisons to some of the greatest players in chess history. Former British champion Keith Arkell, after playing her in 2022 when she was seven, said he "won only because of her inexperience." International Master Lawrence Trent wrote in December 2023 that "I have no doubt she will be England's greatest player and most likely one of the greatest the game has ever seen."

Both players are expected to represent England in future international competitions. Sivanandan already played on England's women's team at the 2024 Chess Olympiad in Budapest at age nine — the youngest person ever selected for a full England team in any sport.
